{"id": 196, "title": "legalbench-rule-application pack — Client letter: Ostrander Tooling multi-forum suit intake (jurisdiction scenarios)", "doc_type": "client_letter", "related_shape": "legalbench-rule-application", "body": "OSTRANDER TOOLING WORKS, INC.
Canton, Ohio — Office of the President

To the Civil Procedure Group, Whitlock & Deene LLP:

Ostrander Tooling Works, Inc. is an Ohio corporation with its only plant and headquarters in Canton, Ohio; treat Ostrander as a citizen of Ohio and domiciled in Ohio for all scenarios. We have four forum questions. Please analyze each

args.rationale: Applying the operative personal jurisdiction memo to Scenario 2 of the Ostrander intake letter (proposed Ohio suit against Brumfeld Freight Lines, a Georgia carrier). Brumfeld is not domiciled in Ohio, so general jurisdiction fails. Under the memo's specific-jurisdiction test, Brumfeld lacks purposeful contacts: it has no operations, customers, or employees in Ohio and solicits no business there; its only connection is a single driver transiting Ohio on an unrelated Pennsylvania-to-Kentucky route, which the memo expressly excludes as merely fortuitous transit. Nexus also fails because the loading-dock injury claim arose entirely at Brumfeld's Savannah, Georgia terminal and does not arise out of or relate to any Ohio contact. Because the defendant is not domiciled in the forum and both the purposeful-contacts and nexus prongs fail, the memo's rule of decision confirms personal jurisdiction is lacking. Determination: rejected.
